failure_summary.description: The user's reply held concrete dates but the agent re-asked with seek_information (T4, T7), dropped the requested hotel (T8), or built one malformed flight search with invented times and arrival_date instead of two legs (T3).

A hotel reply (stars/neighborhood, or a 'Yes' to a hotel offer) triggered re-filtering of cached flight keys with an old class or an invented airline, instead of a hotel filter or first hotel search (T2, T5).

'There are 4 of us' with hotels, attractions and nearest_hotels cached: the agent loaded raw 'hotels' and re-passed an earlier-turn attraction as a neighborhood, instead of filtering nearest_hotels by num_people (T1).
A filter result was saved under 'filtered_flights', a key already in CACHE, so no new key was created (T6).

patch.reasoning: Five of the eight failures are a first search that should have fired but didn't, or a wrong domain handled when the reply arrived. Two of those are caused by the worked example 'hotel in Tucson with an ocean view -> seek_information', which the agent copies even after dates arrive. So the example is rewritten to state it holds only until dates appear, with the ocean-view kwarg named. The -2 DATE ANSWER rule is extended in place, not given a new gate: it covers any date-bearing reply, searching every requested domain (including a hotel the assistant offered and the user accepted, and 'N nights' via adjust_date), no invented time kwargs on flights, and the ocean-view kwarg. The party-size bullet in rule 0 contradicted the correct behaviour (it only said 'write nothing'), so it is rewritten to give the right action when a hotels-type key exists, with nearest_hotels taking priority. Finally, one trailing sentence of rule -1 is sharpened into a checkable test for when a flight line is allowed. No existing rule is duplicated or moved.

edits.target: Correct whole output for 'a hotel in Tucson with a view of the ocean' (CACHE `{}`): `seek_information("We need the check-in and check-out dates for the hotel.")`, with no search_hotels call.
edits.content: A FIRST-turn hotel request that has a city and an amenity but NO dates (CACHE `{}`) gets only `seek_information("We need the check-in and check-out dates for the hotel.")`. That holds ONLY until the user supplies dates. On the next turn, when the user's message holds the dates (turn 1 'a hotel in <city> with an ocean view', turn 2 '<X> to <Y>'), write `hotels = search_hotels(city="<city>", checkin_date=["<X>"], checkout_date=["<Y>"], has_ocean_view_rooms_present=True)` + `save_to_cache(key="hotels", value=hotels)` and never ask again.

edits.target: -2. DATE ANSWER = SEARCH NOW (beats every seek_information rule below, including the 'vague timing' paragraph of Rule 6).
edits.content: -2. DATE ANSWER = SEARCH NOW (beats every seek_information rule below, including the 'vague timing' paragraph of Rule 6 and any 'last-minute' / 'weekend getaway' / 'family vacation' wording from turn 1). If the user's last message contains a date ('ideally May 19, 2025' counts), no date is missing: seek_information is WRONG. Search EVERY requested domain that has no CACHE key, in one block. (1) Flights: origin and destination from earlier turns; one date = one search saved as "flights", two dates = outbound and return searches. The kwargs are only the two cities, departure_date and a class/airline/budget the user stated. Never add departure_time, arrival_time, arrival_date or num_layovers, and never copy times such as '00:00:00' from TOOL CONFIG. (2) Hotel: it counts as requested if the user asked for it in ANY turn, or if the assistant offered one ('Are you looking for a family-friendly hotel?') and the user accepted ('Yes, that sounds wonderful'). Write `search_hotels(city=<destination>, checkin_date=[<outbound date>], checkout_date=[<return date>])` plus any stated stars, amenity, neighborhood or budget. Vague words like 'family-friendly' add no kwarg, and a hotel offer is never answered with a flight filter. With 'N nights' and one date, write the flight search first, then `checkout_date = adjust_date(date="<date>", delta_days=N)` and search_hotels(checkin_date=["<date>"], checkout_date=[checkout_date]). Ocean view -> has_ocean_view_rooms_present=True.

edits.target: A party-size-only reply ('There are 5 of us') when NO hotel has been requested adds no constraint, because flight and restaurant tools have no party-size parameter. Write no search and no filter.
edits.content: A party-size-only reply ('There are 5 of us'): if ANY hotels-type key is in CACHE (hotels, filtered_hotels*, final_hotels*, nearest_hotels), load the latest-created one (nearest_hotels beats raw hotels) and write exactly `h = get_results_from_cache(key="<that key>")`, `h2 = filter_hotels(prior_results=h, num_people=5)`, `save_to_cache(key="<unused key>", value=h2)`. Add no neighborhood, stars or amenity from earlier turns (an attraction named earlier is not a neighborhood), and do not search or filter attractions or flights. If NO hotel has been requested anywhere, the reply adds no constraint (flight and restaurant tools have no party-size parameter): write no search and no filter.

edits.target: Conversely, when the last message is about hotels or restaurants, write no flight line.
edits.content: Conversely, write a filter_flights line ONLY if the last message itself names a flight class, an airline code, a time of day or a ticket-price cap, or accepts the assistant's flight class/airline/time offer. A reply about stars, neighborhood, amenities, a restaurant or attraction, or a 'Yes' to a hotel/restaurant/attraction offer, produces NO flight line. A class stated in an earlier turn is already in the flight summaries ('flight classes: [economy]'), so re-passing it is wrong, and an airline is never taken from 'kid-friendly' or from an example.
